As of 300 AM Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Patchy dense fog and low clouds will reduce 
visibilities early this morning across portions of central NC, with 
the lowest visibilities and most persistent fog focused across the 
Sandhills and Coastal Plain.

Calm winds and high low level moisture early this morning will help 
fog and low cloud development through daybreak. While patchy fog is 
possible farther west in the Piedmont, the thickest fog and lowest 
cloud cover will develop across the Sandhills and Coastal Plain. 
Visibilities could drop to a quarter mile or less at times during 
the morning commute, especially along and east of US1 creating 
localized pockets of dense fog. Morning sunlight will quickly burn 
off the fog, returning mostly clear skies/high clouds to the region 
by mid morning. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... Temperatures will remain well above average ahead 
of a cold front that will move south across cntl NC on Sat.

A sub-tropical high, centered over GA in 700-500 mb upr air data at 
00Z/1st and with observed heights around the 90th percentile at GSO, 
will progress offshore today and settle across the swrn N. Atlantic 
through the weekend. 

At the surface, a ~1020 mb high now centered about halfway between 
Bermuda and the NC coast will drift to near Bermuda, while extending 
wwd across the Southeast, through Fri. Subsidence from the 
subtropical ridge aloft, and sly, "return" flow around the Bermuda 
surface high, will contribute to additional warming of the airmass 
over the Carolinas and a couple more days of summerlike 
temperatures. While hotter by day, and gradually more humid/muggy by 
night, afternoon humidity levels will remain relatively low and in 
the 30s to 40s percent courtesy of mixed/afternoon dewpoints that 
will again decrease mostly into the mid-upr 50s this afternoon and 
low-mid 60s F Fri afternoon. 

KEY MESSAGE 3... Cloudy, much cooler, and periods of wet conditions 
will develop in cold air damming later Sat through the weekend.

A positively-tilted srn stream trough/shear axis will progress 
slowly across the Southeast and Carolinas this weekend, just 
downstream and equatorward of a series of prominent shortwaves that 
will progress through a broad trough that will become centered over 
ern Canada. The models have trended slower and more amplified with 
one of those shortwave troughs forecast to dig from the nrn Rockies 
to the OH Valley through the weekend and which will likely favor a 
period of enhanced lift over cntl NC Sat night-early Sun night.  

At the surface, high pressure extending from near Bermuda to the 
South Atlantic coast will be displaced by a wavy frontal zone 
forecast to settle swd and across cntl NC on Sat, then stall and 
become quasi-stationary from SC to southeastern NC Saturday night. A 
following, ~1028-1030 mb cP high will progress across and offshore 
sern Canada this weekend, while extending swd across the Middle 
Atlantic and Carolinas. Though progressive, the high will be 
favorably strong and located for cold air damming to develop over 
the srn Middle Atlantic and Carolinas. The associated wedge front 
may buckle nwd across ern NC with the passage of a weak frontal wave 
Sun into early Sun night. 

Initially patchy and light rain, in the developing damming regime 
and nely flow on Sat, will become steadier and increase in intensity 
Saturday night and Sunday. It will do so as mass response, ahead of 
the aforementioned nrn stream shortwave trough that has trended more 
amplified in model guidance during the past 24 hours, accelerates 
the flow and strengthens isentropic upglide across the frontal zone 
and atop the CAD high. Although there remains uncertainty in storm 
total rainfall amounts, it appears increasingly likely that a 
relatively widespread, soaking rain will result over cntl NC by the 
end of the weekend. As confidence in that pattern (probably) 
continues to increase in the coming days, forecast high temperatures 
and diurnal ranges for Sat night-Sun night will probably require 
additional adjustments downward from currently forecast NBM/WPC 
ones. In fact, if the previously noted pattern indeed occurs, 
temperatures on Sun will likely be very similar to the distribution 
of 60s F that occurred in the recent cold air damming episode of 
9/23. 

A reinforcing cold front and following cP/Canadian surface high will 
progress across the srn Middle Atlantic early next week, with 
following cool and dry fall conditions for cntl NC through at least 
mid week.
